title: Tweezer
hook: Walk one atom array through a day, engine by engine.
sub: A day in the life of a neutral-atom quantum computer, told by a chain of Atlas engines, with signal survival measured at every hop.
you_control: Walk the lab: tap any of the 18 pixel-art stations (or Earlier / Later) and Tweezy, an atom in a tweezer beam, walks there while the lab clock sweeps to that hour

Play each stage's scene, drawn from its real output: load attempts, snap the camera, set the photon threshold, run the moves, drag atoms, pick Rydberg patterns, check the error-corrected pets, play the xylophone score and the echo
Flip any stage to Data for its charts and engine frames; copy a link to any stage
Judge each hop: survival F against chance, on Tweezy's face, the stage gauge and the survival curve
qubits_note: 210 = tamagotchi-v1: 30 Steane logical qubits x 7 data qubits on Aer's stabilizer simulator. 156 = the most qubits that ran on IBM ibm_fez (comet-qrng-v1: 148-qubit register + 8 Bell-witness qubits, the whole Heron chip). 7 of the 8 hardware-capable stages ran on IBM ibm_fez (5 Oct 2026, same inputs as the recorded day) and are the primary results on the page: coin-toss-v1 1 qubit, job d27e51b3-464d-48d6-97ca-97b2bb49072a; comet-qrng-v1 156 qubits, job 7a6587bb-9185-4038-a7d2-fab4c5a87193; qpixl-v1 qubits not reported, job e3b9dbd1-8919-4667-a048-a5e112f7f6be; labyrinth-v1 20 qubits, job a8fdcac4-4a50-4168-a3b7-2c11826c6f09; graph-v1 20 qubits, job 216de0ea-ca8a-4b01-8a89-6b071eaa6048; retrocausal-echo-v1 24 qubits, job 4839781c-7d2b-4926-aa4b-23a62800f4c0; otoc-echo-v1 24 qubits, job 18aa3832-83ff-46f1-b66a-d5c756895591. Did not complete on ibm_fez: tessa-image-v1 (2 tries: ed0a2239, 56cdf27d, The engine did not respond in time — retry the job). Kept beside them as labelled comparisons (they fed the later stages): the recorded hardware runs on ibm_marrakesh (coin-toss-v1 1 qubit, job 83ad70dc; comet-qrng-v1 156 qubits, job f7749ef9) and the recorded emulator runs of the other ibm_fez stages. Other stages ran at their engine ceilings where the platform allowed: 24 (echo engines, Aer cap for the exact runs; the ibm_fez echo runs use the same 24-site chain so the two compare site by site), 21 (teleblur; shader budget), 20 (blur, graph, labyrinth, blur-midi, qdrive), 19 (blur-core, payload-limited), 16 per deep-fryer tile; qrc-image and qpixl do not report a count.
honesty: Atlas runs gate-model circuits and simulators, not atoms: every stage is a labelled analogy; only completed jobs are counted and every failure is listed with its job ID.
